(a) 
The amendments made by the several sections of this title shall be effective on the enactment date of this Act except as otherwise provided herein.
 
    (b) 
The amendments made by sections 102(a) and 105(h) shall be effective with respect to determinations of recovery from disability made on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (c) 
The amendments made by sections 102(b) and 102(c) shall be effective with respect to months after the month of enactment.
 
    (d) 
The amendments made by section 102(d) shall be effective with respect to recomputations made, or changes in law enacted, on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (e) 
The amendments made by sections 103(b) and 105(k) shall be effective with respect to annuities awarded on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (f) 
The amendments made by section 103(c)(1) shall be effective with respect to annuities accruing in or after the month of enactment.
 
    (g) 
The amendments made by sections 103(c)(2), 103(f), and 105(f) shall be effective with respect to awards made on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (h) 
The amendments made by section 103(e) shall be effective with respect to months after the month in which this Act is enacted.
 
    (i) 
The amendments made by sections 105(a), 105(b)(1), and 105(j)(2) shall be effective with respect to annuities accruing for months after 1964 where, pursuant to the next sentence, no application for the annuity is required or, if required, such application is filed within one year after the month of enactment of this Act; otherwise, the twelve-month limitation on retroactivity, provided for in section 5(j) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1937, shall apply. In the case of an individual who is not entitled to a child’s insurance annuity under section 5(c) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1937 for the month in which this Act is enacted, such amendments shall apply only on the basis of an application filed in or after the month in which this Act is enacted; except that no application shall be required of a child age eighteen to twenty-one, inclusive, with respect to whom the Board has information on the date of enactment of this Act of his eligibility for an annuity under the amendments made by section 105(j)(2) of this Act through the application of section 3(e) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1937.
 
    (j) The amendments made by section 105(c)(1) shall be effective with respect to lump-sum payments awarded on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (k) 
The amendments made by section 105(c)(2) shall be effective with respect to deaths occurring in or after the twelfth month preceding the month of enactment.
 
    (l) 
The amendments made by section 105(d) (1) shall be effective with respect to deaths occurring on or after the enactment date of this Act.
 
    (m) 
The amendments made by section 105(g) shall be effective with respect to deductions made in the calendar year 1966 and thereafter.
 
    (n) 
The amendments made by section 105(j) (1) shall be effective with respect to annuities under section 5(c) of the Railroad Retirement Act for months after the month in which this Act is enacted; except that in the case of an individual who was not entitled to an annuity under section 5(c) of such Act for the month in which this Act was enacted, such amendment shall apply only on the basis of an application filed in or after the month in which this Act is enacted.
 
    (o) 
The amendment made by section 105(j) (3) (i) shall be effective with respect to annuities for months after the month of enactment of this Act. No lump-sum benefit under section 5(f) (2) of the Rail-road Retirement Act of 1937 shall be awarded after the date of enactment of this Act in any case in which an individual survives who would be entitled to an annuity under the amendment made by this section unless such individual executes an election in accordance with such section 5(f) (2) before attainment of age 60 to have such benefit paid in lieu of other benefits.

fable.w: The section only sets effective dates for amendments to the Railroad Retirement Act and says when an annuity application is required. The tempting reading is that references to applications filed with the Board, or an individual executing an election, involve outside parties in a federal decision. Under the definition, applications for benefits are not participation, and nothing here provides for consultation, comment, hearings, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: such amendments shall apply only on the basis of an application filed in or after the month in which this Act is enacted

qwen_block.w: This section solely defines the effective dates and temporal scope of various statutory amendments. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The mention of 'applications' refers to individuals applying for benefits, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The amendments made by the several sections of this title shall be effective on the enactment date of this Act except as otherwise provided herein.

opus.w: This section only sets effective dates for amendments to the Railroad Retirement Act. Its only outside-party actions are individuals filing applications for annuities and making elections about lump-sum benefits. Both are benefit applications or choices, which the definition excludes, not consultation on a federal decision. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty, or right to sue.
opus.s: such amendments shall apply only on the basis of an application filed in or after the month in which this Act is enacted
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is that the references to individuals filing "an application for the annuity" and executing "an election" to take a lump sum count as outsiders taking part in a federal decision. That reading fails against the definition. Applying for benefits is expressly excluded. Choosing a lump sum over an annuity is just picking a benefit; it is not consultation on a government decision. The rest of the section only sets effective dates. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section details the effective dates of various amendments and specifies when applications for benefits must be filed. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with states/tribes before making a decision; rather, it outlines procedural rules for individuals to claim benefits.
qwen_chat.s: The amendments made by sections 105(a), 105(b)(1), and 105(j)(2) shall be effective with respect to annuities accruing for months after 1964 where, pursuant to the next sentence, no application for the annuity is required or, if required, such application is filed within one year after the month of enactment of this Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for individuals to file applications or execute elections constitutes "participation" because it involves outside parties interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." Furthermore, these are administrative procedures for claiming entitlements, not consultations or coordination on federal policy decisions.
